prompt: rgb.jpg is a horizontal strip of 5 frames, left to right in time order, sampled from the few seconds of a head-mounted (egocentric) video; the camera wearer is the viewpoint. depth.jpg, segmentation.jpg and pose.jpg are the same 5 frames rendered as a monocular depth map (brighter = nearer to the camera wearer), an instance segmentation map (coloured masks with class labels), and a body/hand skeleton map (yellow = body, magenta = hands) on black. Look at all four images. For EACH of the three maps, describe the spatial understanding that map supports, using the RGB strip for context: the layout of the scene; which people and objects are present and roughly how far each is from the camera wearer (in metres) and from each other; relative positions (left/right/in front/behind, above/below); which way people face and whether they look toward the camera wearer; what is within arm's reach of the camera wearer or of others; occlusions and anything partly out of view; and how these change across the 5 frames (approach, retreat, turning). Say what each map shows that is hard to see in the RGB alone, and where the map looks unreliable. Describe only spatial facts. Do not guess anyone's intentions, social norms, or what anyone should do. Return only JSON: {"depth": "...", "segmentation": "...", "pose": "..."} with 3-5 sentences each.

descriptions.depth: The depth map shows a top-down egocentric view where the camera wearer stands directly above a triangular trailer tongue toolbox (about 0.6–1.0 m below the head) attached to a vehicle bumper on the left and a wooden trailer bed on the right, with asphalt ground at roughly 1.5–1.7 m below. The brightest regions are the wearer's own torso and shoulders at the bottom edge (0.2–0.4 m away) and their arms extending down into arm's reach (0.5–0.8 m) to open the toolbox lid in frames 2–3 and grasp a coiled strap inside in frames 4–5. A second person is barely visible in frame 1 at the top left (about 2.5–3.0 m away), approaches from the upper left in frame 4 (hand entering at ~0.8 m), and reaches into the toolbox in frame 5 (0.5–0.9 m from the camera wearer and ~0.3 m from the wearer's left hand), oriented sideways toward the toolbox with their head and upper torso cropped out of view. Compared to the RGB strip, the depth map clearly separates the foreground raised toolbox lid, vertical jack post, and overhanging torso from the recessed ground plane without confusion from dark shadows or black paint. However, the depth map is unreliable inside the open toolbox in frames 3–5, where the tangled chains and straps are smoothed into an indistinct mid-grey blob, and along thin hitch chains where fine depth discontinuities are lost.
descriptions.segmentation: The segmentation map outlines the camera wearer's lower torso, legs, and arms at the bottom of all five frames (0.2–0.8 m away, facing forward/downward toward the trailer tongue), as well as the second person approaching on the upper left in frames 4 and 5 (0.5–1.2 m away, positioned to the left of the toolbox and reaching right into the compartment within arm's reach of the wearer). Across the sequence, the wearer's segmented left arm shifts forward to lift the triangular lid in frame 2 and reaches into the open compartment in frames 3–5, while the second person's arm and bent legs enter from the top-left edge in frames 4–5 to grasp the same strap. While the masks help isolate the overlapping limbs of the two people at the bottom and left edges from the dark pavement, the map is heavily unreliable for object recognition and boundaries. It misclassifies the trailer bed and tongue as an 'airplane' in frame 1, labels the triangular metal toolbox as an 'umbrella' in frame 2, and mislabels the open toolbox lid and internal chains/straps as 'person' masks in frames 3 and 5. Furthermore, it completely fails to segment the trailer, hitch, and toolbox in frame 4, leaving the entire non-person scene black.
descriptions.pose: The pose map renders only magenta 3D hand skeletons in the first three frames and contains no yellow body skeletons across any of the five frames because both people's heads and full bodies are largely out of the downward-looking field of view. In frame 1, it detects the camera wearer's right hand resting on the trailer frame (about 0.6 m away, bottom right), and in frames 2 and 3 it tracks both the wearer's left hand (centre-left, 0.6–0.7 m away) and right hand (centre-right, 0.5–0.7 m away, separated by ~0.3–0.4 m) as they grasp the toolbox latch and prop open the lid within easy reach. This skeletal rendering makes the exact finger articulation and pinch grip of the wearer's hands in frames 1–3 easier to read than in the high-contrast RGB image, especially where the left hand in frame 2 is over dark metal. However, the pose map is completely unreliable in frames 4 and 5, where it outputs an entirely black image and fails to detect any hands or bodies despite the camera wearer's hands and the approaching second person's left arm and legs being clearly visible and interacting with the strap at 0.5–1.0 m distance.
